title: Persistent Effort
note: He defines ஆள்வினை as unbroken, real effort. Getting rid of laziness is not enough, because work is only carried out by effort, so this follows the chapter on laziness.

couplets.plain: Don’t lose heart and say “This is too hard.” Effort will give you greatness.
couplets.pm: Don’t look at your own smallness, think that finishing this work is too hard, and lose heart. Effort will give you the greatness to finish it. Keep trying and you become great, and then even hard things are easily done.

links.reason: Effort itself supplies the greatness that a daunted person thinks is missing.

couplets.plain: In any work, take care not to let the work fail. The world leaves those who leave work undone.
couplets.pm: The world leaves those who leave undone the work they can’t do without. So in the work at hand, don’t stop and sit idle.

links.quote: take care not to let the work fail
The world leaves those who leave work undone

couplets.plain: The pride called helping others rests in the fine quality called effort.
couplets.pm: The distinction of doing good to everyone rests in the high quality called effort. Those who make the effort have wealth in hand, so they are the ones able to help. It isn’t found in anyone else.

links.reason: Only one with the quality of effort can know the pride of helping others.

couplets.plain: Helping others, in someone without effort, will come to nothing, like a sword in a eunuch’s hand.
couplets.pm: A man without effort can no more be a helper than a eunuch who fears the sight of weapons can wield a sword among them. The eunuch means to use the sword, but fear stops her. He means to help many, but poverty stops him. Some read வாளாண்மை as valour with the sword.
couplets.sensitive: uses a eunuch as the image of what is useless

links.quote: a sword in a eunuch’s hand

couplets.plain: Someone who wants work, not pleasure, wipes away their kin’s suffering and is the pillar that holds them up.
couplets.pm: One who wants no pleasure for himself but only to finish the work clears the suffering of his kin, his load, and is the pillar that bears it. He can end the poverty of kin and friends and protect them, so he needn’t speak of himself. Whoever wants the cause and not the effect gains everything. Whoever wants the effect and not the cause gains nothing.

couplets.plain: Effort builds prosperity. Lack of effort lets want in.
couplets.pm: The effort of rulers makes their wealth grow, and lack of it brings them poverty. Wealth here means the six parts of a kingdom, and poverty means being without them. Once that happens, their enemies destroy them.

links.quote: Lack of effort lets want in
links.reason: Lack of effort brings in one thing only, and that is want.

couplets.plain: They say dark Misfortune lives in laziness, and she of the lotus in the effort of those without it.
couplets.pm: The dark goddess of misfortune lives in a person’s laziness, and the goddess of fortune in the effort of one who isn’t lazy, say those who know. Her darkness is the darkness of sin, carried over to sin’s fruit.

links.reason: Makes laziness the house where dark Misfortune lives.

links.quote: she of the lotus in the effort
links.reason: Places the lady of the lotus inside the effort of those without laziness.
She of the lotus and dark Misfortune each choose a dwelling by a person’s habits.

couplets.plain: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one. The disgrace is to know what must be known and make no effort.
couplets.pm: Lacking the fate that gives results disgraces no one. The disgrace is to know what must be known, such as your strength, and not do the work. To those who say effort is useless when the gods don’t favour you, he answers that the world blames no one for past deeds, only for present faults. So keep trying.
couplets.note: பொறி can also mean the senses or limbs. The plain reading follows him in taking it as fate.

links.quote: know what must be known and make no effort
The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one
links.reason: Clears whoever tried and lost: lacking a favouring fate is no disgrace.

couplets.plain: Even if god won’t allow it, effort pays the wages of your body’s toil.
couplets.pm: Even if fate keeps the work you tried from giving the result you wanted, the effort pays at least the wages of your body’s pains and isn’t wasted. If god favours it, it gives more than its measure. Either way nothing is lost, so strive and don’t wait on god.
couplets.note: He reads தெய்வம் here as fate.

links.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil
links.reason: Promises effort its wages even when god won’t grant the result.

links.quote: Even if god won’t allow it
links.reason: Answers the sense that god is against you: the effort is still paid.

couplets.plain: Those who strive without faltering and without delay will see the back of fate itself.
couplets.pm: Those who don’t weaken before its resistance, and strive at the work without lapse, will see the back even of the fate that blocks the result. Lapse means flaws in planning, in judging strength and the like, and in action. Fate can block you only once or twice, so those who try many times gain the result.

links.reason: Striving without faltering is what lets a person see the back of fate.

links.quote: see the back of fate itself

ideaLinks.quote: The pride called helping others rests in the fine quality called effort
ideaLinks.reason: The pride of helping others rests in effort and nowhere else.

ideaLinks.quote: Helping others, in someone without effort, will come to nothing
Lack of effort lets want in
Effort builds prosperity. Lack of effort lets want in.
ideaLinks.reason: Effort and its lack are set side by side, one building prosperity and the other letting want in.

ideaLinks.quote: will see the back of fate itself
ideaLinks.reason: Striving without faltering lets a person see the back of fate.
